properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js@1.1.7 is a real declared dependency in this project's package-lock.json (transitive dep of the truffle/web3 toolchain, which is what package.json declares). It ships SHA-1/SHA-224/SHA-256 implementations with the build. No application call site found in src/ or migrations/ — the app's hashing goes through web3 (keccak256). Part of the dependency inventory: what the lockfile ships is what the image runs.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: secp256k1 IS this project's operative signature curve: web3.js (declared dependency) signs every Ethereum transaction sent by src/bot_flashswap.js and src/bot_normalswap.js with secp256k1 ECDSA, and the tiny-secp256k1/secp256k1 packages are its native backends. Observable here, but not replaceable by this repo — the curve is fixed by the Ethereum protocol; migration to a PQ signature scheme is an ecosystem-wide change, not a code change in this project.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: evp_bytestokey@1.0.x is declared in package-lock.json as a transitive dependency of the browserified crypto stack pulled in by truffle 5.x. It reproduces OpenSSL's legacy single-round MD5-based EVP_BytesToKey KDF. No application call site — the app never derives keys this way; it is shipped library surface, not app behavior. Still a declared dependency, so it belongs in the inventory.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge@0.10.0 is declared in package-lock.json as a transitive dependency of truffle 5.3.2 (used by the truffle toolchain). It ships a pure-JS RSA implementation (keygen/encrypt/sign) plus TLS. No application call site in this repo — the arbitrage bots do no RSA; presence of the library in the shipped dependency tree is what the inventory records. Changeable here: the truffle upgrade that replaces it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: dep_scan finding: create-ecdh is declared in package-lock.json, confirming the ECDH dependency is actually installed in the build's node_modules tree (transitive via truffle/web3).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl@0.14.5 (2016 release) is declared in package-lock.json as a transitive dependency of web3 1.3.x (web3-bzz → swarm-js → tweetnacl-auth), which package.json declares directly. It ships Ed25519 (crypto_sign). No application call site — the bots never sign with Ed25519; this is shipped library surface from the web3 stack. Changeable by upgrading web3.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic@6.5.4 is installed as a transitive dependency (web3.js/ethereumjs stack uses it for secp256k1 ECDSA transaction signing — the core signing path of this Ethereum arbitrage bot, since web3 signs every transaction with an secp256k1 ECDSA key). The version 6.5.4 is also an old elliptic release with known vulnerabilities. Quantum-unsafe signature primitive. Changeable only by upgrading the transitive dependency tree.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: X25519 arrives the same way as Ed25519 here: tweetnacl@0.14.5's crypto_box/scalarMult, declared in package-lock.json via web3's bzz/swarm-js chain (tweetnacl-auth). No application call site found; the bots do no key agreement. Shipped dependency-tree surface; changeable only by upgrading the web3 stack.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak-256 (Ethereum's SHA-3 variant) is genuinely operative here, not just vendored: the build/contracts/UniswapV2Library.json sites are compiled keccak256() calls (pairFor computes Uniswap pair addresses by hashing factory+init-code with keccak256), the metadata lines carry solc's keccak256 source hashes, and package-lock.json declares keccak + @ethersproject/keccak256 (used by web3 to hash transactions before secp256k1 signing). Build artifacts are compiled from this repo's own src/contracts

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Lockfile dependency records for the scrypt KDF family: scrypt-js (^3.0.1/^3.0.0/2.0.4, the memory-hard KDF web3's keystore encryption uses) and scrypt-async (^2.0.1). All 9 sites are package-lock.json entries; these packages ship in the installed tree as transitive dependencies of truffle/web3. No direct application call site found — presence is the inventory question here. scrypt itself is quantum-safe (symmetric KDF); the finding is the shipped dependency.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Lockfile dependency records for the pbkdf2 npm package (^3.0.3/^3.0.9/^3.0.17 — the browserify PBKDF2 ponyfill, part of the crypto-browserify stack pulled in transitively by truffle/web3) and its @types/pbkdf2 typings. All 8 sites are package-lock.json entries; PBKDF2 ships in the installed tree. web3's V3 keystore uses PBKDF2 or scrypt to encrypt Ethereum keys. No direct application call site — presence is what the inventory records. PBKDF2 is symmetric/quantum-safe as a KDF.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge@0.10.0 is installed as a transitive dependency in package-lock.json (truffle's tree); it provides AES, TLS/PKI (X.509), RSA and more. The AES reachable through it is quantum-safe symmetric crypto (Grover only halves key strength). No direct application call site found; the lockfile declaration ships it in the build. node-forge 0.10.0 is also an old release with known CVEs (0.10.0 fixed only some).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl@0.14.5's secretbox (XSalsa20 stream cipher + Poly1305 MAC) is declared in the same web3-bzz → swarm-js → tweetnacl-auth chain in package-lock.json. XSalsa20-Poly1305 is pre-NIST construction, superseded in modern stacks by XChaCha20-Poly1305. No application call site — shipped library surface only. tweetnacl itself is the provider object LIB-0469707e (other shard); this is its AEAD algorithm facet.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl (NaCl) is installed per package-lock.json as a transitive dependency; it provides XSalsa20-Poly1305 secretbox, X25519 box key agreement and Ed25519 signing. tweetnacl's primitives are quantum-unsafe for key agreement/signatures. No direct application call site found in the arbitrage scripts; the lockfile declaration is what ships it in the build. Changeable only by upgrading the transitive dependency tree.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge@0.10.0 is a declared dependency in package-lock.json (transitive via truffle 5.3.2's toolchain). It ships pure-JS RSA, X.509, TLS and PKCS implementations. The root-level site is the library presence in the tree; the package-lock.json site is the declaration. No application call site — the arbitrage bots never call node-forge APIs. What ships is what the image runs; changeable by the truffle upgrade that drops it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge@0.10.0 (transitive dependency in package-lock.json, truffle's tree) provides the X.509/PKI machinery — certificate creation, parsing, CSR/PKCS handling. The package ships in the build; no application call site found. Its X.509 certificates authenticate with RSA/ECDSA classical signatures, quantum-unsafe, but the inventory entry is the shipped capability of the dependency.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-js@3.0.1 is the concrete package behind the scrypt sites already inventoried under ALG-c1f8b585 — same logical asset reached by both names (the algorithm entry and the package entry). Same shipped dependency: memory-hard KDF used by web3's keystore encryption, transitively installed.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: sha.js@2.4.11 is declared in package-lock.json as a transitive dependency of the elliptic/web3 stack (SHA-1/SHA-2 implementations; used by create-hash, which elliptic depends on). No direct application call site — the bots hash through web3's keccak256. Shipped library surface; the 2.4.11 pin is old (current is 2.4.11/2.0.x era → superseded).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic@6.5.4 is the concrete package behind the ECDSA object ALG-710f61f0 ("ECDSA via elliptic@6.5.4") — same logical asset reached by both names. elliptic provides secp256k1/secp256r1 ECDSA signing that web3.js uses for Ethereum transaction signing, the core signing path of this arbitrage bot. Old version with known vulnerabilities. Quantum-unsafe signature primitive; changeable only by upgrading the transitive tree.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js@1.1.7 ships as a transitive dependency (used by elliptic and the ethereumjs stack for SHA-2/RIPEMD/keccak hashing). It implements MD5, SHA-1, SHA-2, RIPEMD-160 — MD5/SHA-1 among them are broken hashes, though here the inventory records the shipped library, not a call site. No direct application call found; the lockfile declaration installs it in the build.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: pbkdf2@3.1.2 is the concrete package behind the PBKDF2 object ALG-4de3b020 — same logical asset reached by both names (the algorithm entry and the package entry). Browserify PBKDF2 ponyfill, transitively installed via truffle/web3; used by web3 keystore encryption alongside scrypt. Symmetric KDF, quantum-safe as such.
